directive:
ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE (D-0.5 revise 1/5). Both soundness flags are real and both are FIXABLE without weakening the headline. The rate d*binom(d,k_star)/n survives unchanged. Below is the concrete repair, adjudicated with an external math consult and against the verbatim LaTeX source of arXiv:2208.05553. Apply ALL of it.

===========================================================
(1) FIX def:exposed-order  [reviewer flag C-wellposed #1 — ACCEPTED]
===========================================================
Replace with:
    \bar\beta_d := \min\{\beta, d\},
    k_\star(d,\beta,p) := \max\{ 1 <= r <= \bar\beta_d : \Delta_r(p) \ne 0 \}.
Justification to state: \Delta_1(p) = (1-p) - (-p) = 1 for every p, so r=1 always qualifies and k_star is
ALWAYS well defined for d>=1, beta>=1. Add explicitly: when beta > d, subsets of order > d do not exist in
any N_i, so the effective order is min(beta,d) and nothing else changes. Add the standing convention
d <= n (or replace d by min(d,n)) since a neighborhood cannot exceed the population. State the degenerate
case d=0 separately: all neighborhoods empty, tau_n = 0, minimax risk exactly 0.
Update the symbol table entry for k_\star (space becomes {1,...,min(beta,d)}) and re-derive
lem:symmetric-reduction as: at p=1/2, \Delta_r(1/2) = 2^{1-r} for r odd and 0 for r even, so k_star is the
largest ODD integer <= min(beta,d).

===========================================================
(2) REPLACE def:block-family ENTIRELY  [reviewer flag C-wellposed #2 — ACCEPTED]
===========================================================
The current definition is indeterminate AND the sign-array/Rademacher idea is mathematically WRONG here:
with NO observation noise, discrete coefficient shifts give two induced laws with different supports, which
are then too easily distinguished (and can be mutually singular), so Le Cam gives nothing. Use a bounded
CONTINUOUS random baseline plus the normalized Riesz representer. Full determinate construction:

BLOCK GRAPH. Assume d | n first; set m := n/d. Partition V_n into blocks V_1..V_m of size d and include
EVERY within-block directed arrow including self-loops:
    (j,i) in G_n  <=>  i,j in V_b for some b.
Then N_i = V_b for every i in V_b, and d_i^in = d_i^out = d exactly, so both degree bounds are met with
equality. (Non-divisibility: blocks of size between d/2 and d, losing only (beta)-dependent constants.)

BLOCK SCORE AND ITS ENERGY. On one d-unit block put
    g_d(z) = sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d} [\Delta_r(p)/(p(1-p))^r] * sum_{|S|=r, S subseteq [d]} prod_{j in S}(z_j - p).
By orthogonality of centered Bernoulli monomials,
    A_d := E[g_d(Z)^2] = sum_{r=1}^{\bar\beta_d} binom(d,r) * \Delta_r(p)^2 / (p(1-p))^r,
and since k_star is the largest order with nonzero contrast,
    A_d  \asymp_{\beta,p}  binom(d, k_star).                                  (*)
Introduce A_d as a NEW named definition (call it the block score energy); (*) should be its own small lemma,
because it is the object that carries the binomial factor and it is what replaces the anchor's coarse
sum_{k<=beta} binom(d,k) <= (e d/beta)^beta step.

NORMALIZED REPRESENTER. h_d := g_d / A_d. The Riesz identity for the Bernoulli contrast gives, for every
polynomial f of degree <= \bar\beta_d,  f(1) - f(0) = E[f(Z) g_d(Z)]. Applying it with f = g_d:
    h_d(1) - h_d(0) = 1,        E[h_d(Z)^2] = 1/A_d.
Write h_d(z) = sum_{|T| <= k_star} h_T prod_{j in T} z_j in the RAW monomial basis. State and prove the
uniform-in-d coefficient bound
    H_{\beta,p} := sup_{d>=1} sum_T |h_T| < \infty,
by expanding each centered monomial: numerator and denominator are both dominated, up to (beta,p)-constants,
by their largest nonzero order. This bound is what makes the ell^1 envelope hold ALMOST SURELY.

BOUNDED NUISANCE. Let s := B/2 and let U_1..U_m be i.i.d. across blocks with density
    f_s(u) = (1/s) cos^2( pi u / (2s) ) * 1{|u| <= s},
chosen because sqrt(f_s) has finite translation Fisher energy  ||(sqrt f_s)'||_2^2 = pi^2/(4 s^2).

TILT AMPLITUDE.  delta := c_{\beta,p} * B * min{ 1, sqrt( d*A_d / n ) },  with c_{\beta,p} > 0 small enough
that delta * H_{\beta,p} <= B/2.

THE TWO PRIORS. For sigma in {-1,+1} define Pi_sigma: draw U_1..U_m i.i.d. from f_s, and for every i in V_b
    c_{i,T} = U_b * 1{T = empty}  +  sigma * delta * h_T      for |T| <= k_star,
all other coefficients zero. Then the envelope holds a.s.:
    sum_T |c_{i,T}| <= |U_b| + delta * sum_T |h_T| <= B/2 + B/2 = B.
IMPORTANT framing point to state explicitly: U_b is PRIOR RANDOMIZATION OF FIXED POTENTIAL-OUTCOME
COEFFICIENTS, not exogenous observation noise. The construction remains inside the noiseless design-based
model. (This is exactly the property the anchor's earlier sigma>0 version lacked — see (5) below.)

SEPARATION. Under Pi_sigma, for every realization, Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) = sigma*delta*(h_d(1) - h_d(0)) =
sigma*delta, hence tau_n = sigma*delta almost surely, so |E_{Pi_+} tau_n - E_{Pi_-} tau_n| = 2*delta. This is
a genuine determinate opposite-tilt pair (it is what the reviewer asked for).

DIVERGENCE — USE HELLINGER, NOT KL. Within block b all d observed outcomes coincide:
    Y_i^obs = U_b + sigma*delta*h_d(Z_b),  i in V_b.
Conditional on Z_b = z the two laws are translates of f_s by +- delta*h_d(z), so by the L^2 translation
inequality
    H^2( f_s(. - delta h_d(z)), f_s(. + delta h_d(z)) ) <= 4 delta^2 h_d(z)^2 ||(sqrt f_s)'||_2^2
                                                        <= (pi^2 delta^2 / s^2) h_d(z)^2.
Averaging over Z_b and using E[h_d^2] = 1/A_d gives  H_b^2 <= 4 pi^2 delta^2 / (B^2 A_d). The m = n/d blocks
are independent, so Hellinger tensorization gives
    H^2(P_+, P_-) <= 4 pi^2 n delta^2 / (B^2 d A_d).
Hence TV is bounded away from 1 exactly when delta^2 <~ B^2 * d*A_d/n \asymp B^2 * d*binom(d,k_star)/n, and
two-point Le Cam yields
    R_n^\star  >~_{\beta,p}  B^2 * min{ 1, d*A_d/n }  \asymp  B^2 * min{ 1, d*binom(d,k_star)/n }.
In the saturated regime d*A_d/n >~ 1 take delta = c_{\beta,p} B; the bound above is still O(1).
STATE THE REASON for Hellinger over KL: the two densities are compactly supported translates, so one-sided
KL can be INFINITE (supports do not coincide), while Hellinger is quadratic in the translation. Do not
route this converse through KL.

WHY THE BINOMIAL SURVIVES (this belongs in the proposal as the mechanism paragraph). The anchor puts
independent variance of order 1/binom(d,beta) on each order-beta coefficient; the induced outcome variance
then grows with the number of exposed subsets and CANCELS the same combinatorial factor, which is precisely
why their bound is d-free. Here instead the nuisance is a single common random constant U_b per block and
the tilt direction is the NORMALIZED contrast representer h_d, which satisfies contrast(h_d) = 1 and
E[h_d^2] = 1/A_d \asymp 1/binom(d,k_star). A contrast displacement of size delta therefore produces only
design-averaged squared observational displacement delta^2/A_d; that inverse energy is exactly what leaves
binom(d,k_star) in the rate. The EXTRA SINGLE FACTOR d is block replication permitted by the out-degree
constraint: one latent coefficient schedule contaminates d receivers, leaving only m = n/d independent
experimental blocks.

===========================================================
(3) UPPER BOUND — state the two improvements as DISTINCT
===========================================================
Do not describe the gain as one lump "factor d". There are two separate, independently statable gains:
  (i) BINOMIAL vs d^beta. Replace the coarse sum_{r<=beta} binom(d,r) <= (e d/beta)^beta by the exact
      weighted score energy A_i = sum_{r <= min(beta,|N_i|)} binom(|N_i|,r) \Delta_r(p)^2/(p(1-p))^r <= A_d,
      with A_d \asymp binom(d,k_star). This is where the exposed-order cancellation is harvested.
 (ii) ONE out-degree factor, not d_in*d_out. The overlap identity is
          sum_{l=1}^n binom(|N_i \cap N_l|, r) = sum_{|S|=r, S subseteq N_i} #{ l : S subseteq N_l },
      and for every nonempty S,  #{ l : S subseteq N_l } <= min_{j in S} d_j^out <= d, so
          sum_{l=1}^n binom(|N_i \cap N_l|, r) <= d * binom(|N_i|, r) <= d * binom(d, r).
      So the real overlap cost is a SINGLE out-degree factor d. The in-neighborhood combinatorics are
      ALREADY inside binom(d,r) and must not be charged again as a separate d_in prefactor. THAT double
      charge is the anchor's extra factor of d.
Target variance statement: Var(tauhat_SNIPE) <= C_{\beta,p} B^2 d A_d / n. Make the overlap identity its own
lemma — it is the load-bearing combinatorial step of the upper bound.
Saturation: since |tau_n| <= B, the zero estimator (or clipping SNIPE to [-B,B]) gives the B^2 branch, so
R_n^\star <~ B^2 min{1, d binom(d,k_star)/n}. Keep the min{1,.} on BOTH sides.

===========================================================
(4) HONESTY CORRECTION on the k_star < beta claim — DO NOT OVERCLAIM
===========================================================
It is FALSE that order-beta coefficients are invisible to every estimator at p=1/2 with beta even. Explicit
counterexample to avoid: beta=2, Y(z) = c z_1 z_2 is plainly observable when Z_1 = Z_2 = 1 and is estimable
by an exposure-weighted estimator. Do NOT write "invisible", "undetectable", or "carries no information".
The TRUE and sufficient statement is: \Delta_beta(1/2) = 0 means the order-beta centered monomial does not
appear in the RIESZ REPRESENTER OF THE ALL-ONE VERSUS ALL-ZERO CONTRAST; that contrast's dependence on
order-beta structure is carried through lower centered orders. Hence the DESIGN-INDUCED SCORE COMPLEXITY
for this particular estimand is governed by k_star rather than by the maximal model order beta. Phrase the
headline slogan accordingly: the degree order is set by the order the design EXPOSES IN THE CONTRAST
REPRESENTER, not by the model order. Any stronger phrasing is an overclaim and will be caught downstream.

===========================================================
(5) ANSWER strengthening path #3 BY CITATION — the ell^1 envelope is NOT a new condition
===========================================================
The reviewer asks to justify the ell^1 coefficient envelope or else redo everything in the published
bounded-outcome class. Neither is needed; it is answerable from the anchor's own text. VERBATIM from the
LaTeX source of arXiv:2208.05553 (file s3_model.tex), the anchor's own normalization is
    Y_max := max_{i in [n]} sum_{S' subseteq S_i^beta} |c_{i,S'}|
followed by "It follows that |Y_i(z)| <= Y_max for any treatment vector z."
So ass:bounded-coefficient-mass IS the anchor's Y_max, i.e. EXACTLY the constant appearing in their
Theorem 1. State this explicitly with the citation. Consequences to write down:
  - Our UPPER bound is therefore over precisely the anchor's Theorem-1 class, so the claimed factor-d
    tightening is a like-for-like comparison, not a change of class.
  - ell^1-bounded IMPLIES outcome-bounded (|Y_i(z)| <= sum_S |c_{i,S}| <= B), so the ell^1 class is a SUBSET
    of the bounded-outcome class used by EichhornKhanUganderYu2026. A minimax LOWER bound over a SMALLER
    class is the STRONGER statement and immediately implies the lower bound over the larger bounded-outcome
    class. So our converse is not weakened by the choice of class -- it is strengthened. Say so.
This removes the "borderline" published-axis concern without new mathematics.

===========================================================
(6) SCOPE / CONSTANT HONESTY — add to honest_scope
===========================================================
State the standing conditions d >= 1, beta >= 1, d <= n (or d -> min(d,n)); general n needs a routine
unequal-block argument. State plainly that constants depend only on (beta,p) FOR FIXED beta and
p in (0,1), but are NOT uniform as p -> 0 or p -> 1, and degrade when a nonzero \Delta_r(p) approaches zero.
Do not claim uniformity in p.

===========================================================
(7) POSITIONING / PROSE SYNC
===========================================================
lem:symmetric-reduction was called "incremental" against the anchor's Eq. (4.4). Keep it, but present it
explicitly as an ILLUSTRATIVE COROLLARY of thm:degree-frontier (the p=1/2 specialization), NOT as an
independent contribution; the contribution is the frontier itself plus the exposed-order object.
Sync tldr, project_justification.{gap,niche,fill} and related_work to the repaired statement: the headline is
the matched two-sided frontier B^2 min{1, d binom(d,k_star)/n} with k_star over min(beta,d), whose converse
is a NOISELESS bounded-coefficient block construction. Useful positioning fact for related_work, verifiable
in the anchor's own source: an earlier version of their Theorem 2 was d-DEPENDENT but required exogenous
observation noise sigma > 0, and carried the remark that "when sigma=0, the minimax lower bound is
meaningless ... it would be interesting to see if one could relax this assumption and prove a minimax lower
bound result directly on the noiseless setting." The published version bought noiselessness by giving up
d-dependence. This proposal gets BOTH, which is precisely the gap they flagged. Only assert this if the
reviewer-facing text can support it from the accessible author version.

ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE (D-0.5 revise 2/5). The three reviewer flags are accepted and all three are fixable.
An external math consult additionally found FIVE further defects the reviewer did not flag, INCLUDING one
real soundness bug in the headline display, and it PROVED that the d|n restriction can be removed outright
(a strengthening, not a caveat). Apply everything below in ONE pass. Do not fix these one per round --
this is a single wholesale hygiene/domain audit over all nodes.

===========================================================
(A) d = 0 CONVENTION  [reviewer flag 1 — ACCEPTED]
===========================================================
Adopt k_star(0,beta,p) := 0 and binom(0,0) := 1. Then d*binom(d,k_star)/n at d=0 equals 0*1/n = 0, which
matches R*_n(0,beta,p,B) = 0 exactly, so the frontier display stays CORRECT AND UNIFORM down to d=0 and the
theorem can be stated for 0 <= d <= n with no separate branch inside the display.
Use this wording for the conventions block:
  "For d=0, set betabar_0 = 0, k_star(0,beta,p) = 0, binom(0,0) = 1, and interpret sums over nonempty
   subsets as zero. The assignment space {0,1}^0 consists of the single empty vector and the empty product
   equals 1. Set g_0 = 0, A_0 = 0, and, purely as an empty-object convention, h_0 = 0; the notation
   h_0 = g_0/A_0 is not used. All normalized-representer identities are asserted only for d >= 1. If d = 0,
   every N_i is empty, hence Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) = 0, tau_n = 0, and R*_n(0,beta,p,B) = 0."
CRITICAL: A_d \asymp_{beta,p} binom(d,k_star) is FALSE at d=0 (A_0 = 0 but binom(0,0) = 1). So
lem:block-energy-representer keeps a d >= 1 hypothesis, as do h_d = g_d/A_d, E[h_d^2] = A_d^{-1},
h_d(1)-h_d(0) = 1, the lower-bound mixture argument, any division by d*A_d, and the Riesz program.
Remove the trailing "If d=0, ..." sentence from INSIDE thm:degree-frontier and put it in the conventions
block; the theorem display then needs no exception.

===========================================================
(B) DELETE THE d | n RESTRICTION -- IT IS PROVABLE, NOT A CAVEAT  [reviewer flag 2 — RESOLVED BY STRENGTHENING]
===========================================================
Do NOT restrict the corollary to d|n. Do NOT leave the unequal-block extension in honest_scope as unproved.
The general-n construction works for EVERY 1 <= d <= n. Write it into the lower-bound proof sketch:
  Let m := floor(n/d), q := m*d, rho := q/n. Partition q units into m blocks of size d with all within-block
  arrows including loops; make the remaining n-q units ISOLATED with all coefficients zero (inert).
  Active i in block b keeps c_{i,T} = U_b*1{T=empty} + sigma*delta*h_{d,T}; inactive units get zero.
  The envelope still needs only delta*sum_T |h_{d,T}| <= B/2.
  Since h_d(1)-h_d(0) = 1, the estimand becomes tau_n = sigma*delta*(md/n) = sigma*rho*delta, so the
  separation is 2*rho*delta. Only the m active blocks contribute to the likelihood, so
      H^2(P_{-1},P_{+1}) <= 4 pi^2 m delta^2 / (B^2 A_d).
  Choose delta^2 = eta_{beta,p}^2 B^2 min{1, A_d/m}. Le Cam gives R*_n >~ rho^2 delta^2.
  KEY ELEMENTARY FACT that closes it: floor(u) >= u/2 for u >= 1, hence 1/2 <= rho <= 1 for every
  1 <= d <= n. With x := d*A_d/n one has A_d/m = x/rho, and
      rho^2 * min{1, x/rho} >= (1/4) * min{1, x},
  with a matching universal upper constant. Therefore R*_n >~_{beta,p} B^2 min{1, d*A_d/n}
  \asymp_{beta,p} B^2 min{1, d*binom(d,k_star)/n}, with NO residual divisibility condition.
  The d > n/2 regime is NOT a danger zone: there m=1 but rho = d/n > 1/2 so dilution is mild, and
  d*binom(d,k_star)/n >= d/n > 1/2 (since binom(d,k_star) >= 1), so that regime is saturated up to
  constants and the min{1,.} branch carries it.
The UPPER bound never used divisibility at all -- it is a whole-graph variance calculation from the degree
and overlap bounds only. Say so explicitly.
Restate thm:degree-frontier for "integers n >= 1 and 0 <= d <= n", no divisibility hypothesis, and delete
the unequal-block sentence from honest_scope. lem:symmetric-reduction then no longer needs d|n either.

===========================================================
(C) SOUNDNESS BUG IN THE HEADLINE DISPLAY -- PLAIN SNIPE IS NOT THE ATTAINING ESTIMATOR  [NOT reviewer-flagged; FIX IT]
===========================================================
The middle inequality currently names the PLAIN, UNCLIPPED SNIPE estimator and sandwiches it above by
C_{beta,p} B^2 min{1, d binom(d,k_star)/n}. That is NOT justified: in the SATURATED regime plain SNIPE need
not satisfy a uniform O(B^2) risk bound -- its variance bound is the unsaturated expression, and nothing
caps it at B^2. The min{1,.} upper branch requires an estimator that is actually bounded.
Repair (choose the first, it is cleanest):
  Define the clipped estimator  tauhat^up := Pi_{[-B,B]}( tauhat_SNIPE ), the projection onto [-B,B].
  Since |tau_n| <= B (immediate from the ell^1 envelope), clipping cannot increase squared error, and the
  clipped error is at most 4B^2. So tauhat^up satisfies BOTH branches of the min.
State the honest two-regime version so no strength is lost:
  - in the nonsaturated regime d*binom(d,k_star)/n <~ 1, PLAIN SNIPE attains the rate;
  - uniformly over all regimes, the CLIPPED SNIPE tauhat^up attains B^2 min{1, d binom(d,k_star)/n}.
Either name tauhat^up in the middle of the display, or define the SNIPE estimator to include the clipping
from the outset -- but do not leave plain SNIPE sandwiched by a bound it does not satisfy. (An equivalent
acceptable device: switch between SNIPE and the zero estimator according to the KNOWN value of
d binom(d,k_star)/n; note this is legitimate because d, beta, p, B are known to the analyst.)

===========================================================
(D) REPLACE def:riesz-program -- IT IS CURRENTLY THE WRONG PROGRAM  [reviewer flag 3, root cause]
===========================================================
Two distinct programs are being conflated; the one written down is neither. Let P_d := span{z_S : |S| <=
betabar_d} and L_d(f) := f(1) - f(0).
  (i) NORMALIZED PERTURBATION program (this is what h_d is, and what the lower-bound tilt direction needs):
          min_{h in P_d} E[h(Z)^2]  subject to  h(1) - h(0) = 1.
      Unique solution h_d = g_d/A_d, optimal value A_d^{-1}.
  (ii) UNBIASED WEIGHT program (this is what an estimator weight is):
          min_{w in L^2(P_Z)} E[w(Z)^2]  subject to  E[w(Z)] = 0 and E[w(Z) Z_S] = 1 for all nonempty S
          with |S| <= betabar_d.
      Unique minimum-norm solution w = g_d, optimal value A_d.
The currently written program has the nonempty-S constraints but OMITS E[h] = 0; it is feasible (the
monomial Gram matrix is nonsingular for p in (0,1)) but it neither enforces unbiasedness for the intercept
nor defines the normalized perturbation. Replace def:riesz-program by whichever of (i)/(ii) each use site
needs -- state BOTH if both are used, under distinct names, and say which is which. The representer identity
E[g_d(Z) f(Z)] = L_d(f) for all f in P_d, with A_d = E[g_d^2], should be stated explicitly since it is what
makes both programs solvable in closed form.

===========================================================
(E) DETERMINATE OEQ  [reviewer flag 3 — ACCEPTED]
===========================================================
Replace the OEQ with the following determinate version (it fixes estimator class, regime, and equivalence
relation). Keep it close to this wording:
  "Fix beta >= 1, p in (0,1), B > 0. Let n_t, d_t -> infinity be integer sequences with d_t | n_t and
   d_t*A_{d_t}/n_t -> 0. Let G_t be the disjoint union of n_t/d_t complete directed blocks of size d_t, with
   loops. Let E_t^{loc,lin} be the class of estimators tauhat_{w,t} = n_t^{-1} sum_i w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)}) Y_i(Z)
   where each w_{i,t} in L^2(P_Z) is measurable with respect to the assignment in i's own block only, and the
   estimator is design-unbiased for tau_{n_t} over the whole model class -- equivalently E[w_{i,t}] = 0 and
   E[w_{i,t} Z_S] = 1 for every nonempty S subseteq N_i with |S| <= betabar_{d_t}. Put
   R_t^{loc,lin} := inf_{tauhat in E_t^{loc,lin}} sup_{M_t} E[(tauhat - tau_{n_t})^2].
   Determine whether lim_t R_t^{loc,lin} / (B^2 d_t A_{d_t}/n_t) exists and, if so, its value. In addition,
   characterize all asymptotically minimax sequences, where asymptotic minimaxity means
   sup_{M_t} E[(tauhat_{w,t} - tau_{n_t})^2] / R_t^{loc,lin} -> 1; specifically, is asymptotic minimaxity
   equivalent to (n_t A_{d_t})^{-1} sum_i E[(w_{i,t}(Z_{b(i)}) - g_{d_t}(Z_{b(i)}))^2] -> 0, up to relabeling
   coordinates within blocks?"
Note WHY the class is restricted to block-local linear unbiased estimators: covering arbitrary measurable or
nonlinear unbiased estimators would additionally require asserting that their linear/Hajek projections exist
and are the objects compared; without that, "arises from a Riesz minimizer" is undefined. Say this in one
sentence so the restriction reads as deliberate, not as a gap.
For exact-constant questions use the proxy d*A_d/n, NOT d*binom(d,k_star)/n -- the latter is equivalent only
up to (beta,p)-dependent constants and so cannot pin a leading constant.

===========================================================
(F) REMAINING AUDIT ITEMS -- fix all, none is reviewer-flagged
===========================================================
1. SELF-LOOPS ARE LOAD-BEARING. The block construction needs the graph class to ALLOW self-loops and to
   count each loop toward BOTH in- and out-degree; otherwise a complete block on d units has degree d-1 and
   every index shifts. State this globally in ass:bounded-degree (the anchor CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023
   also permits self-loops, i in N_i, so this is not an extra assumption -- cite it as theirs).
2. BASIS OF h_T. Specify that h_d = sum_T h_{d,T} z_T is expanded in the RAW MONOMIAL basis and that
   sum_T |h_{d,T}| is the raw-monomial coefficient sum. The ell^1 envelope is a raw-coefficient condition,
   so this must not silently mean centered-Bernoulli coefficients.
3. B = 0. The nuisance density has scale s = B/2 and is undefined at B = 0. Either assume B > 0 throughout
   the mixture proof, or state the theorem for B >= 0 and dispose of B = 0 separately (there the class is
   the single zero model and R* = 0).
4. Write h_d(1_d) - h_d(0_d) = 1 with the dimension marked; at d = 0 those two vectors coincide.
5. lem:overlap-count is valid at d = 0 too, provided l ranges over V_n and out-degree means
   #{l : j in N_l} <= d. The hypothesis r >= 1 IS essential -- keep it.
6. lem:symmetric-reduction: "k_star is the largest odd integer <= min(beta,d)" needs d >= 1. Make it inherit
   EXPLICITLY n >= 1, 1 <= d <= n, p = 1/2 and the theorem's assumptions rather than inheriting silently;
   handle d = 0 by the convention in (A).

===========================================================
(G) POSITIONING
===========================================================
Novelty is now clear on BOTH axes -- do not add comparators or rewrite related_work. Keep
lem:block-energy-representer, lem:overlap-count and lem:symmetric-reduction explicitly labelled as SUPPORTING
technical steps (the reviewer correctly calls them incremental against the anchor's Eq. (4.4) and Appendix B);
the contribution is thm:degree-frontier plus the exposed-order object k_star. Do not oversell the lemmas.
Sync tldr / project_justification / honest_scope to the strengthened scope: the frontier now holds for ALL
0 <= d <= n with no divisibility condition, and the attaining estimator is clipped SNIPE (plain SNIPE in the
nonsaturated regime). Remove the now-obsolete unequal-block caveat from honest_scope; keep the p-uniformity
caveat and the "vanishing even-order contrast does not mean the coefficient is unobservable" caveat.

ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTIVE (D-0.5 revise 3/5). All three flags accepted. Flag 1 is a framing error introduced by
my own earlier directive and I am correcting it here with the precise replacement text. Apply all of (A)-(D).

===========================================================
(A) COMPARATOR FRAMING -- RETRACT THE "WE BEAT THEIR THEOREM 2" CLAIM  [N-mischar — ACCEPTED, my error]
===========================================================
The reviewer is RIGHT. The anchor's Theorem 2 draws coefficients from unbounded Gaussian priors, so its
realizations violate any fixed ell^1 envelope and it is NOT a lower bound over the Y_max <= B coefficient-mass
class. It must not be presented as a like-for-like bounded-class comparator.
